    CHAIN_ROTATION_TOLERANCE
    Tolerance for each element of the body to ECEF rotation matrix when comparing against the chained navigator oracle: elements are bounded by one and both sides execute the same operations, so differences are bounded by accumulated rounding (1e-13 after 1000 samples).

    Tolerance, in meters per second, when comparing velocity against the truth or the chained navigator oracle: the navigator velocity update is the exact inverse of the kinematics estimation, so only rounding errors (below 1e-9 m/s) remain.

    private static final double
    EPOCH_POSITION_TOLERANCE
    Maximum position error, in meters, right after a Kalman epoch fed with error-free pseudo-ranges of a moving body, as required by the issue: the body moves up to 15 m between epochs, so an epoch using measurements at a timestamp other than their own leaves errors of several meters, while a correct one leaves the solution on the truth.

    private static final double

    Tolerance, in meters, for the displacement of a free fall of up to 1 s starting with a speed of up to 3.5 m/s (2 m/s per axis) against v0 * t + g * t^2 / 2.
    private static final double
    FREE_FALL_VELOCITY_TOLERANCE
    Tolerance, in meters per second, for the velocity of a free fall of up to 1 s starting with a speed of up to 3.5 m/s against v0 + g * t: the neglected Coriolis acceleration (1.9e-3 m/s^2 at most, see FREE_FALL_POSITION_TOLERANCE) integrates to 1.9e-3 m/s; hence 5e-3 m/s.

    ROTATION_ANGLE_TOLERANCE
    Tolerance, in radians, for the angle rotated by the body with respect to the ECEF frame during up to 1 s against the measured angular rate times the elapsed time: the gyroscope measures the rotation with respect to the inertial frame, which differs by the Earth rotation (7.29e-5 rad/s, i.e. at most 7.29e-5 rad after 1 s); hence 1e-4 rad, which is three orders of magnitude below the rotations of up to 0.3 rad being tested.

    (package private) void
    testClosedLoopTracksTruth()
    Checks the closed loop on a trajectory with speed and heading changes, tactical grade IMU errors and noisy pseudo-ranges every second: after convergence the position error stays below three standard deviations of the GNSS position accuracy, it ends up smaller than the error of the INS-only solution for the same data, and it is consistent with the estimated covariance.

    testConstructor()
     
    (package private) void
    testEpochGateAcceptsExactInterval()
    Checks the epoch gate of GNSS measurements: measurements arriving exactly one epoch interval apart are accepted, while measurements arriving earlier, or repeating a timestamp, are ignored.

    testEveryImuSampleCountsWithinEpoch()
    Checks that IMU samples arriving within a Kalman epoch interval are all integrated: with a 1 s epoch interval and 100 Hz samples of a body that accelerates and then decelerates, the solution must equal the per-sample integration, not a single step using only the last sample.

    testMeasurementsAreUsedAtTheirTimestamp()
    Checks that GNSS measurements are used in a Kalman epoch at their own timestamp: for a body whose speed and heading change, error-free 100 Hz kinematics and error-free pseudo-ranges every second, no Kalman epoch is run between measurements and the position error right after each epoch is below 0.5 m.

    Checks that propagate never uses again GNSS measurements already consumed by a Kalman epoch (it returns false and leaves the state untouched), and that it runs the pending epoch when measurements were provided before the estimator was ready to propagate.

    (package private) void
    testRotationIsIntegrated()
    Checks that the angular rate of every IMU sample is integrated: after a 10 s trajectory yawing at 0.1 rad/s, with GNSS measurements provided only at the start, the estimated yaw must be 1 rad.
    (package private) void
    testTranslationIsIntegrated()
    Checks that the specific force of every IMU sample is integrated: after moving north at 10 m/s for 10 s, with GNSS measurements provided only at the start, the estimated position and velocity must be the true ones (up to the accuracy of the GNSS initialisation), and must equal the per-sample integration from the initialised solution.
    (package private) void

    (package private) void
    testUpdateMeasurementsWithoutKinematicsAndWithoutInitialAttitude()
    Checks that GNSS measurements provided to an estimator without attitude and without kinematics initialise position, velocity and clock and run the first Kalman epoch: the solution is the true one, the attitude remains the default one, and repeating the timestamp makes no action.

    • YAW_TOLERANCE

      private static final double YAW_TOLERANCE
      Tolerance, in radians, for the yaw integrated over the yawing trajectory. The kinematics generated by ECEFKinematicsEstimator are the exact inverse of the attitude update of ECEFInertialNavigator up to rounding errors, which after 1000 samples remain several orders of magnitude below this value; 1e-6 rad (0.2 arc-seconds) is far below the 1 rad that is lost when rotation is not integrated.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • DIFFERENT_POSITION_THRESHOLD

      private static final double DIFFERENT_POSITION_THRESHOLD
      Minimum distance, in meters, for two solutions to be considered different: three orders of magnitude above the tolerance of the chained navigator oracle, and well below the 0.5 m that separate the per-sample integration from a single step using only the last sample.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • CHAIN_POSITION_TOLERANCE

      private static final double CHAIN_POSITION_TOLERANCE
      Tolerance, in meters, when comparing against the chained navigator oracle. Both sides execute the same floating point operations, so differences can only come from rounding of ECEF coordinates of magnitude 6.4e6 m (ulp of 1e-9 m).
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • CHAIN_VELOCITY_TOLERANCE

      private static final double CHAIN_VELOCITY_TOLERANCE
      Tolerance, in meters per second, when comparing velocity against the truth or the chained navigator oracle: the navigator velocity update is the exact inverse of the kinematics estimation, so only rounding errors (below 1e-9 m/s) remain.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • CHAIN_ROTATION_TOLERANCE

      private static final double CHAIN_ROTATION_TOLERANCE
      Tolerance for each element of the body to ECEF rotation matrix when comparing against the chained navigator oracle: elements are bounded by one and both sides execute the same operations, so differences are bounded by accumulated rounding (1e-13 after 1000 samples).
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • GNSS_POSITION_TOLERANCE

      private static final double GNSS_POSITION_TOLERANCE
      Tolerance, in meters, for the position of a solution initialised from error-free GNSS measurements against the truth. The least squares estimator and the Kalman epoch do not predict pseudo-ranges with exactly the same approximations as the measurements generator, which leaves a measured error of about 3 cm after the initialisation, plus the drift caused by the initial velocity error (see GNSS_VELOCITY_TOLERANCE) over at most 10 s; 0.1 m bounds both with margin while being three orders of magnitude below the 100 m lost when translation is not integrated.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • GNSS_VELOCITY_TOLERANCE

      private static final double GNSS_VELOCITY_TOLERANCE
      Tolerance, in meters per second, for the velocity of a solution initialised from error-free GNSS measurements against the truth: for the same reason as GNSS_POSITION_TOLERANCE a measured error of about 1.3 mm/s is left after the initialisation; 5e-3 m/s bounds it with margin.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • ABSOLUTE_ERROR

      private static final double ABSOLUTE_ERROR
      Tolerance when comparing coordinate transformations that must be equal up to rounding: the attitude is re-orthonormalised after each Kalman epoch, which only introduces rounding errors (1e-15) on elements bounded by one.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • HALF

    • FREE_FALL_POSITION_TOLERANCE

      private static final double FREE_FALL_POSITION_TOLERANCE
      Tolerance, in meters, for the displacement of a free fall of up to 1 s starting with a speed of up to 3.5 m/s (2 m/s per axis) against v0 * t + g * t^2 / 2. The neglected Coriolis acceleration is at most 2 * 7.29e-5 rad/s * (3.5 + 9.8) m/s = 1.9e-3 m/s^2, i.e. 1e-3 m after 1 s, and the gravity gradient over the 8.4 m travelled adds 3e-6 s^-2 * 8.4 m = 2.5e-5 m/s^2; hence 1e-2 m.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • FREE_FALL_VELOCITY_TOLERANCE

      private static final double FREE_FALL_VELOCITY_TOLERANCE
      Tolerance, in meters per second, for the velocity of a free fall of up to 1 s starting with a speed of up to 3.5 m/s against v0 + g * t: the neglected Coriolis acceleration (1.9e-3 m/s^2 at most, see FREE_FALL_POSITION_TOLERANCE) integrates to 1.9e-3 m/s; hence 5e-3 m/s.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • ROTATION_ANGLE_TOLERANCE

      private static final double ROTATION_ANGLE_TOLERANCE
      Tolerance, in radians, for the angle rotated by the body with respect to the ECEF frame during up to 1 s against the measured angular rate times the elapsed time: the gyroscope measures the rotation with respect to the inertial frame, which differs by the Earth rotation (7.29e-5 rad/s, i.e. at most 7.29e-5 rad after 1 s); hence 1e-4 rad, which is three orders of magnitude below the rotations of up to 0.3 rad being tested.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • EPOCH_POSITION_TOLERANCE

      private static final double EPOCH_POSITION_TOLERANCE
      Maximum position error, in meters, right after a Kalman epoch fed with error-free pseudo-ranges of a moving body, as required by the issue: the body moves up to 15 m between epochs, so an epoch using measurements at a timestamp other than their own leaves errors of several meters, while a correct one leaves the solution on the truth.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • testUpdateMeasurementsWithoutKinematicsAndWithoutInitialAttitude

      @Test void testUpdateMeasurementsWithoutKinematicsAndWithoutInitialAttitude() throws com.irurueta.navigation.LockedException, com.irurueta.navigation.NotReadyException, INSGNSSException, com.irurueta.navigation.frames.InvalidSourceAndDestinationFrameTypeException
      Checks that GNSS measurements provided to an estimator without attitude and without kinematics initialise position, velocity and clock and run the first Kalman epoch: the solution is the true one, the attitude remains the default one, and repeating the timestamp makes no action.
      Throws:
      com.irurueta.navigation.LockedException - if estimator is locked.
      com.irurueta.navigation.NotReadyException - if estimator is not ready.
      INSGNSSException - if estimation fails.
      com.irurueta.navigation.frames.InvalidSourceAndDestinationFrameTypeException - never thrown.

    • testUpdateMeasurementsWithBodyKinematicsAndWithoutInitialAttitude

      @Test void testUpdateMeasurementsWithBodyKinematicsAndWithoutInitialAttitude() throws com.irurueta.navigation.LockedException, com.irurueta.navigation.NotReadyException, INSGNSSException, com.irurueta.navigation.frames.InvalidSourceAndDestinationFrameTypeException
      Checks that an IMU sample provided before any GNSS measurement only sets the time reference (there is no position to navigate from), and that measurements provided afterwards initialise the solution to the true one and run the first Kalman epoch.
      Throws:
      com.irurueta.navigation.LockedException - if estimator is locked.
      com.irurueta.navigation.NotReadyException - if estimator is not ready.
      INSGNSSException - if estimation fails.
      com.irurueta.navigation.frames.InvalidSourceAndDestinationFrameTypeException - never thrown.

      Checks the behaviour of body kinematics updates once the solution has been initialised with GNSS measurements: the first sample only sets the time reference (no navigation, no Kalman epoch), a repeated or older timestamp is ignored, and the second one is integrated with the ECEF inertial navigation equations over the elapsed interval (position, velocity and attitude).

      Returns:
      solution of the estimator before and after integrating the second sample.
      Throws:
      com.irurueta.navigation.LockedException - if estimator is locked.
      com.irurueta.navigation.NotReadyException - if estimator is not ready.
      INSGNSSException - if estimation fails.
      InertialNavigatorException - if the oracle navigation fails.
      com.irurueta.navigation.frames.InvalidSourceAndDestinationFrameTypeException - never thrown.
